record.paper_title: Confinement of color: open problems and perspectives.
record.original_question: In finite-temperature QCD with dynamical quarks, is the deconfining transition an order-disorder transition associated with an exact vacuum symmetry and a genuine order parameter, or is it only a crossover in which quantities related to free quarks, such as the quark abundance ratio n_q/n_p and the inclusive quark-production cross section σ_q, become extremely small in the low-temperature phase without being exactly zero? Equivalently, is color confinement an absolute property of the vacuum enforced by symmetry, or only a very strong dynamical suppression of free quarks across a crossover?

evidence.quote: The "natural " explanation is that nq and σq are strictly zero , or that confinement is an absolute property of vacuum based on symmetry.
An "unnatural" alternative also exists compatible with a crossover: nq and σq very small but not identically zero in the confined phase and there is no order parameter.

A fundamental issue to understand confinement in QCD is whether the deconfining transition is order -disorder or can be a crossover , i.e. whether confinement is an absolute property of the vacuum based on symmetry or is a dynamical change of physical quantities like nq of Eq(1) or σq of Eq(2) by several orders of magnitude across a crossover.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at finite temperature with dynamical quarks of physical masses. Define two physical observables associated with free (colored) quarks:

(i) n_q/n_p, the ratio of the abundance of free quarks to the abundance of protons in thermal equilibrium;
(ii) σ_q, the inclusive cross section for production of a free quark in a hard hadronic collision.

In the high-temperature (deconfined) phase, both quantities are nonzero; experimentally, in the low-temperature (confined) phase, both are bounded above by extraordinarily small numbers (n_q/n_p ≲ 10^{-27} and σ_q ≲ 10^{-40} cm^2).

Two scenarios for the deconfining transition are logically possible:

(A) Order–disorder scenario: There exists an exact symmetry of the QCD vacuum whose spontaneous breaking distinguishes the two phases, with a genuine order parameter that vanishes identically in the confined phase. In this case n_q = 0 and σ_q = 0 exactly below the transition, and confinement is an absolute property of the vacuum enforced by symmetry.

(B) Crossover scenario: There is no exact symmetry and no genuine order parameter; n_q and σ_q are nonzero but extremely small in the low-temperature phase, and they change by many orders of magnitude across a smooth crossover into the high-temperature phase.

Determine which of (A) and (B) is realized in full QCD with dynamical quarks. Equivalently, decide whether color confinement is enforced by an exact (possibly hidden, generalized) symmetry of the vacuum yielding a true order parameter, or is only an extremely strong dynamical suppression of free-quark observables across a crossover.
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains open. With dynamical quarks of physical mass, center symmetry is explicitly broken, so the Polyakov loop is only an approximate order parameter; lattice simulations at zero baryon density show an analytic crossover rather than a sharp transition, but whether an exact (possibly hidden/dual) symmetry underlies confinement and yields a genuine order parameter is still unresolved. Recent studies (e.g., on three degenerate flavors with imaginary isospin chemical potential) construct special setups with exact center symmetry, but the physical-mass case is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Lattice QCD at non-zero temperature and density (Karsch)
status_evidence.snippet: Center symmetry is explicitly broken in the presence of dynamical quarks with finite mass... deconfinement is not expected to be related to a phase transition in QCD with physical quark masses.
status_evidence.claim: In physical-mass QCD center symmetry is broken and the transition is a crossover, with only an approximate order parameter.

status_evidence.title: Exact center symmetry and first-order phase transition in QCD with three degenerate dynamical quarks
status_evidence.snippet: For a specific choice of imaginary isospin chemical potential, QCD with three degenerate flavors possesses an exact center symmetry, intact at low T and spontaneously broken at high T.
status_evidence.claim: Researchers are still actively constructing special settings where an exact symmetry and a genuine deconfining order parameter exist, indicating the general question is open.

status_evidence.title: Phase Transitions in QCD
status_evidence.snippet: There is a crossover transition between the hadronic and quark gluon plasma phases of QCD at zero net baryon density.
status_evidence.claim: Standard view is crossover at physical quark masses, but the symmetry-based interpretation of confinement remains debated.
